title: Study into Ban on Electric Collars for Animal Training
what_it_is: Study into Ban on Electric Collars for Animal Training

sections.label: Electric collar guidelines and enforcement
sections.summary: NParks is developing non-enforceable guidelines on aversive training devices like electric collars, while enforcement under the Animals and Birds Act continues for unnecessary animal suffering.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: As part of the RAWG’s recommendations, the National Parks Board (NParks) further consulted key stakeholders of the animal community and members of the public on the use of electric collars in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: To complement existing guidelines on dog training and behaviour rehabilitation, NParks is currently developing guidelines to highlight the risks of using aversive animal training devices such as electric collars and will share more details when ready.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Ultimately, these guidelines recommend good practices to be adopted by the community and are not meant to be legally enforceable.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding this, in cases where unnecessary pain or suffering is found to be inflicted on animals, we will not hesitate to investigate and take enforcement action under the Animals and Birds Act.

sections.label: Animal cruelty case statistics
sections.summary: From 2019 to 2023 AVS received about 1,250 alleged animal cruelty cases yearly, with about 60 cases per year from 2019 to 2022 found related to animal cruelty.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: On this point, I would like to share with the House that from 2019 to 2023, the Animal and Veterinary Service (AVS) consistently received about 1,250 cases of alleged animal cruelty each year, including feedback from the Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (SPCA).

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Between 2019 and 2022, an average of about 60 cases per year, or 5% of the total, were found to be related to animal cruelty.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Enforcement actions were taken against offenders, ranging from warnings to prosecution, depending on the severity of the case.

sections.label: Reviewing animal cruelty penalties
sections.summary: The Government is considering strengthening penalties for animal cruelty as part of an ongoing review of the Animals and Birds Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: As I mentioned in my Committee of Supply speech, we are looking at the possibility of strengthening penalties for animal cruelty as part of our ongoing review of the Animals and Birds Act.
